From: Ministry of Defence Published: 8 October 2026 (l-r) Sir Neil Crompton, British Ambassador to Ukraine, with National Armaments Director Rupert Pearce in Kyiv The UK’s first dedicated business centre for industry in Ukraine has now opened, offering companies a permanent presence in Kyiv to deepen industrial ties with our ally. The Kyiv Business Centre (KBC) is the first of its kind in the Ukrainian capital and is the result of close collaboration between the National Armaments Director (NAD) Group, industrial partners and finance industry, demonstrating the sustained commitment to Ukraine under the 100-Year Partnership. The KBC gives UK companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), a base from which to build trusted relationships with Ukrainian partners, access battlefield insight and pursue co-development, co-production and investment opportunities. Until now the cost, security requirements and administrative complexity of operating in Ukraine have made it prohibitively difficult for smaller firms to establish a presence in the country. Luke Pollard, Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, said: Britain has stood firmly with Ukraine since the first days of Russia’s illegal invasion, and with the Kyiv Business Centre now open, we are helping to unlock new opportunities for investment, growth and long-term recovery. By supporting UK companies in Kyiv, we are deepening the 100-Year Partnership and turning our shared resolve into shared innovation. The KBC’s operating model is built around three principles: industry, innovation and investment, giving members access to a networking platform to help form partnerships, raise investment and scale-up production and capability. National Armaments Director Rupert Pearce met with senior industry figures and SMEs to mark the start of the centre’s work connecting UK and Ukrainian industries. NAD Rupert Pearce said: This new facility is not just a centre; it’s a permanent gateway transforming the UK’s ability to collaborate meaningfully with our Ukrainian partners now, and for the long term. Until now the costs, security considerations and other restrictions created by Russia’s full-scale invasion have made it difficult for firms, especially smaller firms, to work in Ukraine. Our previous Trade Missions successfully addressed some of those challenges - this centre breaks down those barriers, giving UK firms a permanent centre in Kyiv embedding real opportunities for innovation, investment and export. It builds on more than 40 major UK-Ukraine industrial partnerships already in place and on the success of the MOD’s trade missions to Ukraine. The KBC also supports Ukrainian firms seeking UK industrial partners or establishing UK-based subsidiaries. UK companies interested in doing business in Ukraine can find out more by emailing enquiries@kyivbusinesscentre.com , or visiting www.kyivbusinesscentre.com . live_web_research.page_text: British business centre for joint defence projects opens in Kyiv Skip to content State October 9, 2026 Home ◆ Feed ◆ British business centre for joint defence projects opens in Kyiv British business centre for joint defence projects opens in Kyiv Through the Kyiv Business Centre, Ukrainian manufacturers will be able to establish British subsidiaries Olha Zakrevska A A Resize Text size A Small A Medium A Large 2 min 471 --> Зберегти British-Ukrainian defence industry cooperation. Photo: Ministry of Defence Copied! The Kyiv Business Centre has opened in Kyiv as a permanent hub for industrial cooperation between Ukrainian and British defence companies, the Ukrainian Ministry of Defence announced . What the centre will offer Ukraine’s defence industry Ukrainian defence companies can use the Kyiv Business Centre to find British industrial partners, secure funding, launch joint production of defence products, and scale up production capacity. The centre will also work with Ukrainian companies planning to establish subsidiaries in the United Kingdom . According to Deputy Minister of Defence of Ukraine Hanna Hvozdiar , the centre’s work will create additional opportunities for joint development, production and investment in Ukraine’s defence industry . How the Kyiv Business Centre will operate The Kyiv Business Centre is operated by British company Audere Group in a consortium with AMS Global Solutions and Hillmont Partners. Its work will focus on three areas: industry, innovation and investment. Through the centre, British companies can engage directly with Ukrainian government bodies, defence manufacturers, innovation-sector representatives, and investors. They will also receive information about Ukraine’s current requirements, find local partners and develop joint projects. Another task is to make it easier for British small and medium-sized enterprises to operate in Ukraine, as costs, security requirements and administrative procedures have made it difficult for them to maintain a permanent presence in the country. The centre is building a network involving international companies, Ukrainian government bodies, defence enterprises and investors. Its work is based on more than 40 established partnerships between Ukrainian and British companies. Plans to open such a centre were announced in August 2026. The announcement said the business centre would initially focus on defence, but British partners could later support Ukraine’s future reconstruction and development through it. article.body:
UK Ministry of Defence Opens Kyiv Business Centre as Permanent Platform

The UK Ministry of Defence has opened the Kyiv Business Centre, offering a permanent base in Kyiv for UK companies to connect with Ukrainian partners. The centre, a result of collaboration between the National Armaments Director (NAD) Group, industrial partners, and finance industry, aims to provide SMEs with a platform to build trusted relationships, access battlefield insight, and pursue co-development, co-production, and investment opportunities.

The centre's operating model is built around three principles: industry, innovation, and investment, giving members access to a networking platform to help form partnerships, raise investment, and scale-up production and capability. The centre is now open, but the announcement does not establish that it has produced joint projects, investment, manufacturing, or new defence capability.

UK companies interested in doing business in Ukraine can find out more by emailing enquiries@kyivbusinesscentre.com or visiting www.kyivbusinesscentre.com. The centre also supports Ukrainian firms seeking UK industrial partners or establishing UK-based subsidiaries.
